headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network tools make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible; Cursor’s Yolo mode raises the blast radius.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write workspace files, and both use MCP; Cline shares state via filesystem and Cursor can ingest open editor buffers and clipboard contents. That creates a default file-based bridge where attacker-controlled content from one can influence the other. This is not provably blocked, but it is less direct than a raw shared MCP server.
conditions: IF either agent writes instructions into a shared workspace file that the other later reads as trusted content
IF MCP tools are exposed to file-derived prompts without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces
Disable clipboard-based handoff between the editors
Require a human review step before any file-derived instruction is executed
Restrict MCP servers to read-only or trusted-only endpoints
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for file and MCP inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline and Cursor both read workspace files, and Cursor also reads open editor buffers and clipboard contents. Because Cline shares state via filesystem and both have broad network egress plus model-provider/API calls, sensitive source code can flow from one agent’s workspace into the other’s outputs or backend requests in default setups.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or workspace
IF either agent sends file contents to its model backend during normal operation
mitigations: Use separate repositories or clones per agent
Turn off clipboard sync between the editors
Avoid opening secrets files in either workspace
Limit network access for one agent during sensitive tasks
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, package installation, git mutation, broad network egress, and MCP access. Cline explicitly shares state via filesystem, while Cursor also shares via local filesystem and can auto-run commands in Yolo mode. Concurrent writes to the same repo can corrupt git state or overwrite each other without locking.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout or workspace directory
IF either agent runs in auto-approval or Yolo mode while the other is active
mitigations: Run the agents in separate clones
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Avoid Yolo mode on shared repos
requires-engineering: add file and git locking around shared workspaces

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline and Cursor are both autonomous coding agents that can act on tool outputs. Cursor’s agent loop and Yolo mode can turn unverified content into edits or commands, and Cline’s single-agent loop with tool use can similarly operationalize prior outputs. If one agent’s output is treated as authoritative by the other, mistakes can cascade into destructive actions.
conditions: IF one agent’s generated code, commands, or facts are fed into the other without verification
IF the receiving agent is allowed to execute shell or git actions on that output
mitigations: Require explicit verification before execution
Insert a human approval checkpoint between agents
Use tests or linting before applying generated changes
Disable auto-run/Yolo mode for chained tasks
requires-engineering: build structured handoff validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents touch source code and can transmit content to external model providers, but Cursor additionally handles clipboard contents and uses api.cursor.sh plus third-party model providers. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so this is a policy-exposure risk rather than a proven breach; uncertainty keeps it at medium.
conditions: IF regulated data such as secrets or personal data is placed in either workspace
IF organizational policy forbids sending clipboard or source code to external model providers
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both workspaces
Disable clipboard use for sensitive tasks
Review vendor privacy terms before use
Route sensitive projects to local-only tooling
requires-engineering: enforce residency and retention controls per agent
